sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Christa Pike survived a failed lethal injection on 30 September in Tennessee. Execution staff spent nearly an hour attempting to establish an intravenous line to administer pentobarbital. Pike spent ten days in intensive care suffering from pneumonia, severe swelling and swallowing difficulties before returning to a rehabilitation centre infirmary. She subsequently released a statement describing constant physical pain, mental anguish and isolation, whilst criticising official incompetence.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Pike is believed to be the only person to survive a lethal injection execution attempt. The botched procedure sparked widespread international shock. sections.heading: What happens next

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Google successfully booted up its Project Suncatcher prototype satellite, which launched into orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. Using the onboard Gemma 4 model, the satellite generated its first response, a space-themed haiku, alongside telemetry prompts. The spacecraft carries four Tensor Processing Units, though power limits allow only one to operate at a time.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The project explores whether data centres can operate in space to process distributed AI workloads. Orbit exposes hardware to thermal stress and cosmic radiation, which can trigger bit flips in memory and corrupt data. Google aims to test whether inference workloads remain viable under these real-world conditions rather than ground simulations.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Google will test how the processors withstand orbital conditions before launching two interconnected satellites in 2027. Those future spacecraft will feature higher power generation and optical links.

Loose networks known as The Com target vulnerable young girls on gaming and social media platforms.
Charities and officials warned that these extreme groups represent a grave risk to children online.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Detectives in Scotland joined international efforts to target online gangs known as The Com. These groups groom and coerce vulnerable children, mostly young girls, into acts of self-harm and abuse on gaming platforms and social media. Police have identified victims and perpetrators in Scotland, with one arrest made so far.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts describe the networks as representing the gravest risk to children online. Abusers exploit young people for kudos or clout, escalating harm through manipulation and blackmail. While the scale is considered low-volume, the harm caused is extreme.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Police forces across the UK continue to investigate and map the threat. The Molly Rose Foundation urged action from regulators and leaders, while Ofcom stated it is working closely with law enforcement and will act against services failing to comply with duties.
